title: Provider curation safelist and compatibility policy for Private IaC upgrades
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Upgrades to Terraform providers and shared modules in Private (VPC) deployments have caused subtle runtime incompatibilities during customer upgrades. We need a curated safelist (approved provider + module versions), an automated compatibility matrix, and a documented rollback/playbook so tenant upgrades can be performed with minimal risk and clear observability.

Scope: Produce a canonical compatibility matrix artifact, automation to assert pin conformity in CI, a periodically regenerating recommended pinlist, and an automated health-check bundle to run during canary/rollout windows. This ticket focuses on the governance, automation hooks, and the first curated pinlist for AWS, GCP, Azure provider stacks and our internal redwood-network and redwood-vpc modules.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A machine-readable compatibility matrix (CSV) committed to infra-configs pinned-providers/compat-matrix.csv and referenced from the module registry.
2) CI step fails if a PR changes providers/modules outside approved semver ranges without an explicit upgrade proposal link.
3) A rollback playbook with tested terraform state snapshot and provider rollback command examples saved in Confluence and linked from repo.
4) A smoke test + health-check playbook (script) that runs during canary upgrades and reports to the Console incident dashboard.
5) First curated pinlist (aws, gcp, azurerm providers + redwood-* modules) reviewed by Security and signed off.
implementation_notes:
High-level approach:
- Adopt a single source-of-truth CSV and a generator script (python) that emits both lockfiles and a human readable matrix.
- Use terraform-provider-lockfile where available and generate a lockfile per module set.
- Enforce checks in github actions: changed provider versions => run compatibility-check workflow that cross-references compat-matrix.csv.
- Add a 'pin-review' label to PRs that propose provider/module upgrades; require 2 approvers (Infra + Platform).
- For Private deployments, produce a per-customer recommended pinset in infra-configs/customer-pinsets/<tenant>.yaml during upgrade planning.

Trade-offs discussed: full pinning reduces upgrade velocity; we will allow curated "approved-minor-updates" ranges for low-risk providers (patch/minor only) and require explicit proposal for major bumps. The policy favors safety over speed for Dedicated/Private tenants.

Scripting notes: generator script located at infra/tools/pin-generator.py. It consumes: provider-test-matrix.jsonl (test outcomes), current-terraform-locks/, public provider changelogs. Output: compat-matrix.csv and recommended-pinlist.yml.
rollout_plan:
1) Land compat-matrix.csv and the CI check as a feature-flagged workflow (staged for repo:infra-configs) in canary mode.
2) Run the generator against a set of reproducible test vectors (5 representative tenant configs).
3) Enable enforcement on infra-configs repo only for the first 72h; allow infra-team overrides.
4) After 1 week of stable runs, enable enforcement org-wide for private-vpc repos.
5) During tenant upgrades, run the smoke/health-check bundle and hold rollouts if KV cache or instance provisioning errors exceed thresholds.

Canary success criteria: 0 upgrade-induced infra incidents in canary tenants; CI check false-positive rate < 5%.
rollback_instructions: - If an upgrade breaks: 1) Pause rollout. 2) Apply terraform rollback using saved state snapshot: terraform init && terraform state pull > state-before-rollback.tfstate and then terraform apply -state=state-before-rollback.tfstate with pinned provider versions from compat-matrix. 3) Restore provider plugin versions via provider lockfile: terraform providers lock -platform=<platform> --lockfile=legacy.lock (example). 4) Recreate any necessary networking objects from snapshots in S3. 5) Postmortem and mark provider as blocked in compat-matrix until root cause triaged.
health_checks:
- Pre-upgrade: plan-diff check, provider version validation, automated terraform plan checks with drift detection.
- During canary: automated smoke tests (ping control plane, run 10 inference samples, validate KV cache warm-up, confirm autoscaler attachments).
- Post-upgrade: latency SLO regressions monitor (1-minute bins), error rate over 5 minutes, infra-provisioning failures.
- Health check script: infra/tools/upgrade-health-check.sh (returns machine-readable JSON and posts to Console webhook).
testing_strategy:
- Unit tests for pin-generator and matrix comparator.
- Integration: apply-to-dry-run in a sandbox tenant using terraform workspace + provider lockfile.
- Chaos test: simulate provider plugin API latency and ensure health-checks detect regressions.
- Backwards compatibility matrix tests: run existing post-upgrade smoke suites against all supported module/provider pairs in the CSV.
audit_and_reporting:
- compat-matrix.csv is versioned in git. Every generator run creates a changelog entry under infra/logs/pin-generator/ with the source of truth.
- Weekly automated report posted to the infra-channel with newly observed incompatibilities.
- Security review must sign-off on any provider with known CVEs listed in the matrix.
- Add telemetry events for any CI failure related to provider pin validation (event: infra.pin-validation.fail).
notes:
We will not attempt to automate major provider upgrades; those require a cross-team upgrade proposal with regression test sign-offs. The first pass will cover providers: hashicorp/aws, hashicorp/gcp, hashicorp/azurerm, and internal redwood modules: redwood-vpc, redwood-network, redwood-auth.

Next steps: Miguel to open PR with generator and compat-matrix CSV; Asha to schedule security review for provider CVE checks; infra-test-owner to add smoke-runner tests to sandbox tenants.
